title: Tamsin and the Cover
premise: When a burner phone rings with the voice of Mara Voss — the hostage Jonah Sandoval failed to save three years ago — Jonah is dragged into a conspiracy inside the agency that trained them. The voice belongs to Elena Voss, Mara's twin, an analyst-turned-defector who knows the 'Cover,' a cabal of senior officials, plans to stage a catastrophe at the upcoming Geneva summit and pin it on her. Hunted by the Cover's fixer, Jonah and a ragtag crew of burned colleagues must extract Elena before the summit convenes, discovering along the way that Mara's death was no accident but the Cover's first test. In the end Jonah trades their career for the truth: Elena testifies via the very phone network the Cover built to hide its crimes, the summit collapses into scandal, and Jonah walks away with nothing official — except a found family that finally answers when they call.
about_author: Felix Amberdale is the pen name of a former crisis-line volunteer who spent years listening to strangers talk each other back from ledges. They write thrillers about people who do the right thing in rooms where the rules have been quietly removed.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jonah Sandoval, semi-exiled after the Voss negotiation failure, works deniable cases from a basement office. A burner phone arrives in an evidence box; it rings, and the voice is Mara Voss's. POV: Jonah. Beat: dread wrapped in disbelief — grief given a dial tone.

chapters.title: Three Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present: the botched embassy siege, the shot that killed Mara, the internal review that cleared everyone. Jonah replays the tape until dawn, then answers the phone again. POV: Jonah. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: The caller reveals herself as Elena Voss, Mara's identical twin, calling from a safehouse in Trieste. She claims Mara was murdered to test a deniable-operations program called the Cover, and she has proof. POV: Elena. Beat: cautious alliance between two people grieving the same woman differently.

chapters.title: Cases No One Wants Attributed
chapters.summary: Jonah pulls old files and finds a pattern: every negotiator who touched the Voss case has since died or vanished. Their mentor, Deputy Director Calloway, warns them off with unusual urgency. POV: Jonah. Beat: paranoia taking root in institutional soil.

chapters.title: The Fixer
chapters.summary: Introduce Ade Brandt, the Cover's cleaner, who erases a witness in Rotterdam with chilling professionalism — and is assigned Jonah next. POV: Brandt. Beat: cold competence; the reader meets the true antagonist's hands.

chapters.title: Burned Colleagues
chapters.summary: Jonah assembles help: Priya Nair, a signals analyst fired for asking questions, and Tomás Reyes, a disgraced field medic. The trio triangulates Elena's call through a decommissioned relay network — one built by the agency itself. POV: Priya. Beat: found family forming out of shared exile.

chapters.title: Trieste Rain
chapters.summary: Jonah reaches Elena's safehouse minutes after Brandt's team torches it. A chase through the old port ends with Elena wounded but alive, clutching a drive. POV: Jonah. Beat: the conspiracy turns kinetic; no going back.

chapters.title: What Mara Knew
chapters.summary: On a freighter southbound, Elena decrypts the drive: operational logs showing the Cover rehearsed Mara's death as a live-fire loyalty test. Jonah hears their own voice on the recording, begging Mara to stand down. POV: Elena. Beat: devastation transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Calloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah confronts Calloway, who admits he buried the review — not to protect the Cover, but because his daughter's medical debts made him purchasable. He gives them one name before hanging up forever. POV: Jonah. Beat: betrayal and pity entangled; power corrupts in small installments.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: The Cover's plan surfaces: at the Geneva summit, a staged attack will justify emergency powers across three alliances, with Elena framed as the bomber. Fourteen days remain. POV: Priya. Beat: stakes crystallize from personal to geopolitical.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: In a mountain farmhouse, the four learn to trust: Reyes stitches Elena's wound, Priya builds a ghost network, Jonah teaches Elena how negotiators think. Quiet chapter of banter and nightmares. POV: Reyes. Beat: warmth as counterweight; family chosen under fire.

chapters.title: Brandt Closes In
chapters.summary: Brandt traces a careless ping to the valley. A night raid kills two local contacts; the group escapes through a storm drain, but the drive's backup is lost. POV: Brandt. Beat: hunter's frustration curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Elena confesses a partial truth: she didn't defect voluntarily — the Cover let her run to flush out sympathizers, and she's been transmitting under duress. Trust fractures. POV: Elena. Beat: shame, and the question of whether bait can choose not to be.

chapters.title: Turning the Bait
chapters.summary: Jonah proposes the unthinkable: use Elena's coerced channel to feed the Cover false extraction coordinates. Priya rigs the relay so they control what the hunters hear. POV: Priya. Beat: fear converted into leverage.

chapters.title: Geneva Before Geneva
chapters.summary: Recon in Geneva: the summit venue, the Cover's operational cell embedded in security, and a bomb cache matching Elena's description. Reyes goes undercover as venue medical staff. POV: Reyes. Beat: ticking-clock tension; the enemy is already inside.

chapters.title: Calloway's Silence
chapters.summary: News breaks that Calloway died of 'heart failure.' Among his effects, mailed before his death: a ledger naming the Cover's inner circle — including the summit's security chief. POV: Jonah. Beat: grief hardening into indictment.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Jonah offers the Cover a trade: Elena for the bomb's detonator codes, negotiating over the same burner network, using every trick learned in a decade of hostage work. The Cover accepts — because they plan to kill everyone at the table. POV: Jonah. Beat: the negotiator becomes the hostage.

chapters.title: Twenty Minutes on the Bridge
chapters.summary: The exchange on the Pont de la Machine goes wrong exactly as predicted. Brandt springs the trap; Reyes takes a bullet shielding Elena; Priya floods the relay with the Cover's own incriminating traffic. POV: alternating, rapid cuts. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, everything breaking open.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Wounded, the group fights to the lakefront where a chartered boat waits. Jonah stays behind to hold Brandt off — and wins the exchange not with a gun but with words, convincing Brandt's own second to stand down. POV: Jonah. Beat: climax; justice outside the law achieved through the oldest tool — talking someone back from the ledge.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: At the summit's opening session, Priya hijacks the venue screens: the Cover's logs, recordings, and Calloway's ledger, with Elena narrating live over the burner network. Delegates walk out; arrests begin within the hour. POV: Elena. Beat: catharsis — truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Official inquiries begin; Jonah is offered reinstatement and refuses. Brandt vanishes, a loose thread left deliberately. Reyes recovers; the farmhouse gets new locks and a longer table. POV: Reyes. Beat: bruised peace; costs acknowledged without regret.

chapters.title: Answer When It Rings
chapters.summary: Months later, Jonah keeps the burner charged. It rings: a stranger's voice, another impossible case, someone else the system failed. Jonah looks at the found family around the kitchen table and says yes. POV: Jonah. Beat: resolution as beginning — the work continues, together.
